t.5.38.1: Having heard the words of that great-souled son of Vāyu, Sītā, who resembled a daughter of the gods, spoke words that were for her own good.
t.5.38.2: Seeing you, the bearer of welcome words, O monkey, I rejoice greatly, like the earth whose crops are only half-grown when it receives the rain.
t.5.38.3: Show compassion to me and act so that I, full of longing, may touch that tiger among men with my limbs wasted by grief.
t.5.38.5: When the tilaka mark on my forehead had faded, you placed a tilaka of red arsenic on the side of my cheek; surely you must remember that.
t.5.38.4: And, O best of the monkey hosts, there is the token of Rāma that was given: the reed hurled in anger at the crow, which destroyed one of its eyes.
t.5.38.6: O you who are equal to great Indra and Varuṇa, how can you, so valiant, endure that Sītā has been carried off and lives among the rākṣasas?
t.5.38.7: This celestial crest-jewel has been carefully guarded by me; seeing it in my distress, I rejoice as though I were seeing you, O sinless one.
t.5.38.8: This splendid water-born jewel has been handed over to you by me. Beyond this I shall not be able to live, consumed as I am by grief.
t.5.38.9: For your sake I endure unbearable sorrows and the heart-piercing words of the most dreadful rākṣasīs.
t.5.38.10: For one month I shall sustain my life, O slayer of foes; beyond a month, bereft of you, O son of a king, I shall not live.
t.5.38.11: Terrible is this king of the Rākṣasas, and his gaze upon me is not pleasant; and were I to hear that you were perishing, I would not live for a moment.
t.5.38.12: Having heard the piteous words of Vaidehī, spoken with tears, the greatly radiant Hanumān, son of Māruta, then spoke.
t.5.38.14: Somehow you have been found, lady; this is no time for grieving. This very moment, O beautiful one, you shall see the end of your sorrows.
t.5.38.13: O queen, I swear to you by the truth: Rāma is downcast with grief for you, and with Rāma overwhelmed by sorrow, Lakṣmaṇa is tormented.
t.5.38.15: Those two blameless princes, tigers among men, their resolve kindled by the sight of you, will reduce Laṅkā to ashes.
t.5.38.16: Having slain in battle the cruel Rāvaṇa together with his kinsmen, the two Rāghavas will bring you, O large-eyed one, to your own city.
t.5.38.17: O blameless one, you should give me once more a token of recognition that Rāma would know, one that will awaken his joy.
t.5.38.19: Taking that excellent jewel, the glorious one, best among monkeys, bowed his head to the queen and set about departing.
t.5.38.18: She said, “The finest token of recognition has indeed been given here by me. For once Rāma has seen this very ornament of my hair, your words, O heroic Hanumān, will be worthy of his belief.”
t.5.38.20: Seeing that bull among monkeys, who had resolved to leap away and was growing in size with great force, Janaka's daughter, her face full of tears and wretched, spoke in a voice choked with sobs.
t.5.38.22: You should arrange it so that the mighty-armed Rāghava rescues me from this confinement in a flood of sorrow.
t.5.38.21: O Hanumān, you should convey my wishes for the well-being of all: of the two lion-like brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, and of Sugrīva together with his ministers.
t.5.38.23: And when you have gone into Rāma's presence, tell him of this fierce surge of my grief and of the threats made against me by these Rākṣasas; and may your path be auspicious, O foremost hero among the monkeys!
t.5.38.24: The monkey, to whom the king's daughter had made her purpose known, his aim accomplished and his heart overjoyed, considered that only a little of the task remained, and in his mind he went toward the northern quarter.
